decisions.reason: Local integrability licenses only compactly supported tests. For h=sin(exp(x^2)), h is bounded and h' is tempered by distributional differentiation, but |h'(x)exp(-x^2)|=2|x cos(exp(x^2))| has divergent integral (substitution t=exp(x^2) gives |cos t|/t). Repaired the definition using the unique continuous Schwartz extension of the compact-test functional; density proves uniqueness. The modulation product agrees first on compact tests and then by uniqueness on Schwartz tests. Also corrected the empty-domain suggestion: zero always lies in D_m.

Step 1.1 fixes counting measure on Z as the target; the endpoint coefficient bounds and Parseval therefore interpolate into ell^{p′}(Z), not L^{p′}(T). Corrected the single codomain typo in 3.1. With this correction, compatibility on Lp intersect L1 identifies every coordinate with its integral coefficient, and the p=1 supremum bound and p=2 equality hold. This is a nonfatal notation error with the correct target explicit in the statement, core and concluding steps.

The indicator g lives in frequency space. The old equality ||S_m g||=||M_m g|| does not follow from Plancherel and leaves the lower norm bound unproved. Set f=F_2^{-1}g: surjective isometry gives ||f||=1 and ||S_m f||=||M_m g||>M-epsilon. The superlevel set has a finite positive-measure truncation, while M=0 and null-set changes are treated separately. The domain repair is compatible: m f-hat is L2, so its compact-test distribution has the canonical tempered extension.

F7 overstates the S-prime multiplication interface: a merely locally integrable function need not define a tempered distribution. All actual uses in 4.1 and 5.1 have g and ag in L2 by 2.2, so the repair states this sufficient hypothesis and proves the pairing identity by Cauchy-Schwarz. The rejected overstatement is nonfatal to these licensed applications. Also separated b_s=-2pi|xi|p_s from q_s=b_s F_2 f in 4.2, and explicitly cited positive ball measure for the essential norm. The derivative domination constants 9/(e^2 t^2) and (20/(e^2 t^2))^2 and the two PDE signs check correctly.

The cited bump statement controls support inside U but does not assert compactness when U is an unbounded half-space. Its published proof actually constructs a finite union of bounded supports, so this is a nonfatal omitted compactness justification. Locally repaired 1.3 by taking U=B((N+2)e_j,1), which lies in xi_j>N; closed bounded support is compact by Heine-Borel. The inverse Schwartz transform then supplies f_N and the ratio is at least 2pi N. Also restricted F9 to its actual Schwartz-function use and clarified the domain-qualified F3; no extension is asserted for arbitrary locally integrable functions.

The rejection correctly observes W_s=M_s, but this is a valid explicit import, not circular reasoning or a mathematical defect. The page says it imports the batch-12 characterisation verbatim, and the contract uses that theorem for the bijection and norm. I read the supplier proof: inverse bracket multiplication and the surjective isometry J_s give both directions and uniqueness. All regular distributions actually used here have density g in L2 or <xi>^{-s}g; pairing the latter with phi is finite because <xi>^{-s}phi is Schwartz and Cauchy-Schwarz applies. Thus the notation for a regular tempered density is used only where temperedness and absolute convergence are established, not as a claim about every locally integrable function. No new proof route is required for this sound imported interface.

Part 4 uses the preamble g at order s, but its displayed factor <xi>^{-1} is valid only for the order-(s+1) class. With g_s the actual output is 2pi i xi_j g_s; thus the written exported formula is false. Repaired by explicitly naming g_{s+1}=<xi>^{s+1}F(E_{s+1}U) and using it consistently in 1.4. The bound follows from |xi_j|/<xi> <=1. Bracket cancellation gives the isometric shift; the Laplacian ratio has positive two-sided bounds and differs strictly from 1 on the bump support, proving nonisometry for t nonzero. F3 now justifies regular pairings for every weighted-L2 density used, using Schwartz multiplier continuity and Cauchy-Schwarz.

The punctured unit ball does not contain B(0,1/2). Replacing that witness by B(e_1/2,1/4) proves positivity because every point has radius between 1/4 and 3/4; containment in B(0,2) proves finiteness. This is a nonfatal witness error. Also corrected the prose block bound for negative q to 2^{min(q,0)} <= r^q/k^q <= 2^{max(q,0)}; the already-displayed c3,c4 bounds are correct. Explicit compact-interval Riemann/Lebesgue agreement and monotone convergence now license the polar-to-improper-integral bridge. The tail exponent q=2s+n-1 gives q<-1 exactly at s<-n/2, with logarithmic divergence at equality. F3 is restricted to the actual tempered constant density.
